messages:
Alyssa (CS): FYI — Hightower (enterprise, Dedicated eu-west) reported session loss during a model switch. Sales escalated, says it impacts a live demo this week. Ticket P-3421. @Mike (Eng) @Sean (PM) can you take a look?

Alyssa (CS): Repro steps customer provided:
1) Start session via POST /v1/sessions (session_id=st-9f2c)
2) Send a few messages to redwood-2-large, get responses
3) Request model switch to redwood-2-small via PATCH /v1/sessions/st-9f2c -> returns 200
4) Immediately send another chat request with same session id -> response: 401 {\"error\":\"session not found\"}

Alyssa (CS): Customer attached a snippet of the response and a short log: 
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "session not found",
  "code": "SESSION_MISSING",
  "node": "node-7g-5",
  "time": "2026-03-10T14:22:31Z"
}
```

infra-bot: Support ticket P-3421 created in Zendesk (priority: high) :ticket: 

Jordi (Support): I reproduced something similar on a dedicated replicate with cfg closer to their env. Quick repro notes:
- Used same sequence: create -> chat -> patch model -> immediate chat
- Sometimes returns 200 but subsequent requests see kvcache misses and then SESSION_MISSING
- Small log excerpt: `kvcache: lookup st-9f2c -> miss; session-store: tombstone found`

Mike (Eng): Thanks. A few quick questions to triage:
- Is the customer hitting a single node or LB? (we need the node id if they can repro)
- Which commit/tag/deploy was active? Alyssa you mentioned a deploy around 2026-03-10?
- Can you share the exact request headers + body (they might be dropping X-Session-Id on the switch)

Mike (Eng): To help debug, please ask them to run this curl from their environment (or paste the equivalent):
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDCONN\" -H \"X-Session-Id: st-9f2c\" -H \"X-Debug-Trace: 1\" \
  -d '{\"input\": "hello"}' https://dedicated-eu-west.redwood.ai/v1/chat
```
We need the full response headers and the trace id if any. Also, can you pull the serving node logs for node-7g-5 around 2026-03-10T14:22:xxZ?

Sean (PM): Adding product context: customer uses session pinning to support multi-device continuity; regression here is high-severity for them. Acceptance criteria for any fix: reproduce end-to-end, add unit/integration test to guard model-switch path, and confirm no session tombstone during in-flight switches. We should decide whether this needs a hotfix vs. next sprint.

Alyssa (CS): Confirmed customer is on dedicated and saw the failure after the 2026-03-10 deploy. They gave the request body they used (copied):
```
POST /v1/sessions
{"user_id":"acct-122","mode":"chat"}
PATCH /v1/sessions/st-9f2c
{"model":"redwood-2-small"}
POST /v1/chat (with X-Session-Id: st-9f2c)
```
Response to the last POST included the 401 JSON above. Node id included in response (node-7g-5). Customer also attached trace header `x-rw-trace: tr-88b72`.

Mike (Eng): Good. Based on the quick log snippet this looks like KV cache tombstoning when the session metadata is migrated during model switch. Could be a race: session tombstone set while patch is in-flight. I'll open an internal issue and attempt to reproduce with our scheduled repro harness. For now please ask the customer to include full response headers (especially `x-rw-node` and `x-rw-trace`) and enable debug traces.

Mike (Eng): Triage decision: P1 for eng investigation, but not yet a platform-wide rollback. If we can reproduce reliably and it affects other dedicated customers we will consider a rollback. Will update issue with findings.

Alyssa (CS): I'll collect the headers and the customer's trace, then run the curl with X-Debug-Trace they asked for. Will paste logs here when I have them.

Sean (PM): Thanks — adding to roadmap intake board under "session reliability" and linking P-3421. Next steps: eng investigate -> confirm repro -> decide hotfix.

infra-bot: Internal issue created: RW-issue-5873 (linked to P-3421). Assigned to Mike (Eng).
